The Insurance Authority (IA) has banned Mr Lim Ka Kit (Mr Lim), former technical representative (agent) of an Authorized Institution (Licence number: IC3091), from being an insurance intermediary for nine months in a joint enforcement action with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA).

This joint enforcement action is effected under the Memorandum of Understanding on cross-sector collaboration signed by the HKMA and the IA. Further details can be found at the section titled “Enforcement News” and the Register of Licensed Insurance Intermediaries on the IA website as well as the section titled “Enforcement Actions” on the HKMA website.

The investigation conducted by the HKMA revealed that Mr Lim had pressurised eight clients into acquiring medical insurance coverage via telemarketing despite their requests for time to consider. On two occasions, he went further by inducing the clients to alter their heights and weights for the purpose of meeting relevant underwriting requirements.

Ms Maria Tsui, Head of Enforcement of the IA, said, “This case underscores the importance of ethical selling and treating customers fairly. We would like to thank the HKMA for demonstrating its shared commitment to ensuring that the financial industry focuses on honesty, transparency and integrity to build long-term trust.”

The conclusion of this disciplinary case underlines the importance of acting with high integrity in the distribution of financial products.”

items.summary: HKMA发布《Northern Metropolis Financial…》。正文：will help lower banks’ capital costs, assist these entities in obtaining bank financing, and thereby…
key_points: This measure will help lower banks’ capital costs, assist these entities in obtaining bank financing, and thereby accelerate the implementation of NM projects.

items.source_excerpt:
To further strengthen the banking sector’s financing support for Northern Metropolis (NM) projects, the HKMA proposes to amend the Banking (Capital) Rules to designate government-related entities, including 11 post-secondary institutions and three park companies, as Domestic Public Sector Entities. This measure will help lower banks’ capital costs, assist these entities in obtaining bank financing, and thereby accelerate the implementation of NM projects. The HKMA intends to submit the amendments to the Legislative Council in the first quarter of 2027, with a view to their taking effect in the second quarter of the same year.

The Northern Metropolis Financial Advisory Taskforce (Taskforce), jointly established by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and The Hong Kong Association of Banks (HKAB), convened its third meeting today (10 November). Meeting participants included representatives from the HKMA, HKAB, the Development Bureau, the Education Bureau (EDB), The Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau, the Innovation, Technology and Industry Bureau and 25 participating banks in the Taskforce (see Annex).

At the meeting, the EDB presented the latest development of the Northern Metropolis University Town (NMUT), including the positioning of the three university towns1, development of campus areas and related financial arrangements.

Background

10 November 2026

1 San Tin University Town, Hung Shui Kiu University Town and Ta Kwu Ling University Town.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) published today (6 November) the results of the Survey on Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs)’ Credit Conditions for the third quarter of 2026. According to the survey, SMEs’ credit conditions improved slightly.

Owing to small sample sizes of SMEs with existing credit lines (18% of surveyed SMEs) and with new credit applications (2% of surveyed SMEs) during the quarter, the results could be prone to large fluctuations, and hence should be interpreted with care.

In light of the importance of SMEs to the Hong Kong economy and concerns about potential funding difficulties facing SMEs over the past few years, the HKMA has appointed the Hong Kong Productivity Council (HKPC) to carry out this survey, starting from the third quarter of 2016. This survey is conducted on a quarterly basis, covering about 2,500 SMEs from different economic sectors each time. The results of this survey can help monitor the development of SMEs’ access to bank credit from a demand-side perspective.

The results of this survey should be interpreted with caution.

Similar to other opinion surveys, views collected in this survey may be affected by changes in sentiment due to idiosyncratic events that occurred over the survey period, which can make the results prone to fluctuations.

Readers are advised to interpret the results together with other economic and financial information.

Tender results will be published on the HKMA’s website, the Hong Kong Government Bonds website, Bloomberg (GBHK <GO>) and Refinitiv (IBPGSBPINDEX). The publication time is expected to be no later than 3:00 pm on the tender day.

USM represents an important development in Hong Kong’s securities market infrastructure, facilitates electronic ownership and transfer of securities without paper title instruments, while the existing CCASS central nominee structure will continue to operate.

To facilitate a smooth transition to the post-USM Depository arrangements, the key concepts and related operational changes are set out below.

Under USM, prescribed securities will progressively transition from certificated to uncertificated form. The key highlights of each form are outlined below:

• Participating securities are prescribed securities that have become USM-enabled, allowing legal title to be evidenced and transferred electronically without paper title instruments. Existing physical certificates will remain valid but no new certificates or title instruments will be issued once the securities become participating securities.

• Non-participating securities are securities that have not become USM-enabled and therefore continue to operate under the applicable existing arrangements including certificate-based arrangements where applicable.

In response to the potential cybersecurity risks associated with future advances in quantum computing, the HKMA launched the Quantum Preparedness Index (QPI)1 in July 2026 to assess the banking sector’s preparedness for the quantum-safe cryptography. The initial QPI score of 2.3 out of 10 indicated that, while the sector had begun addressing quantum-related developments, its overall readiness for the transition to PQC remains at an early stage. Co-developed by the HKMA and HKUST, the Toolkit aims to support banks in translating awareness into concrete actions, driving the sector towards full quantum readiness, that is, a QPI score of 10 by 2030.

The collaboration reflects HKUST’s role in advancing understanding of emerging technologies and their implications for business and society. Drawing on the multidisciplinary expertise across cybersecurity, cryptography, finance, economics, corporate governance, and technology applications, HKUST is contributing to one of the critical challenges emerging from advances in quantum computing.

The next step is to help banks translate that understanding into clear responsibilities, informed priorities and practical plans.

Through our collaboration with HKUST and the industry, the Toolkit provides a common foundation that banks can adapt to their own circumstances.
